question.problem: Given that ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are the solutions of the equation $\operatorname{sin}⁡x=-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ for $-\pi <x\le \pi ,$ what is the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}?$
question.worked_solution:
We divide both sides of the equation by $\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ and use the identity $\operatorname{tan}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡x & =-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\ \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x} & =-\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x} \\ \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x} & =-\frac{\sqrt{3}\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}}{\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}} \\ \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x} & =-\sqrt{3} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡x & =-\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(-\sqrt{3})=-\frac{\pi }{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $-\frac{\pi }{3}$ lies inside the given domain, our first solution is ${x}_{1}=-\frac{\pi }{3}.$

To find the other solution, we add $\pi $ to the principal value. Hence,

$$
{x}_{2}=-\frac{\pi }{3}+\pi =\frac{2\pi }{3}
$$

Finally,

$$
{x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}=-\frac{\pi }{3}\cdot \frac{2\pi }{3}=-\frac{2{\pi }^{2}}{9}.
$$
